assays.assay_name: LABORAS home cage observation with DOI challenge
assays.assay_description: Individual mice placed in LABORAS cages with wood-chip bedding; 30 min baseline recording of locomotion and grooming, followed by i.p. injection of DOI (0.5 mg/kg) and another 30 min recording. Behaviours classified automatically from vibration signals by LABORAS software.

application_type.evidence: the mouse received an intraperitoneal injection of DOI (0.5 mg/kg dissolved in physiological saline)

setup_habituation.evidence: After baseline recording of 30 min, the mouse was injected... (baseline served as first exposure, no separate habituation session described)

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice are housed in transparent polycarbonate cages... The cage is placed directly onto the sensor platform

food_restriction.evidence: food and water ad libitum... the upper part of the cage (including the top, food hopper and drinking bottle) suspended in a height-adjustable frame

water_restriction.evidence: food and water ad libitum... the upper part of the cage (including the top, food hopper and drinking bottle) suspended in a height-adjustable frame

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately thereafter, locomotion and grooming were measured in the LABORAS cage for another 30 min.

sample_size.evidence: respective sample sizes are indicated in the figures

outcomes.summary: Acute DOI (0.5 mg/kg, i.p.) reduced locomotion and dramatically increased grooming in WT mice. Male Gpm6b-/- mice showed a clearly blunted response (locomotion reduced only to 42% of baseline vs 17% in WT; smaller grooming/locomotion ratio increase). Female Gpm6b-/- mice showed weaker DOI effects overall, with higher baseline grooming/locomotion ratio than WT.
outcomes.statistics: Males: locomotion maximal reduction WT vs KO p = 0.002 (t-test); grooming/locomotion ratio WT vs KO p = 0.001 (Mann-Whitney U). Females: locomotion maximal reduction p = 0.084; grooming/locomotion ratio p = 0.0012 (t-test).
outcomes.evidence: In WT mice, the time spent with locomotion decreased to 17.42 ± 4.47% of baseline, whereas the maximal reduction in Gpm6b -/- mice reached only 42.12 ± 5.77% (p = 0.002)... male Gpm6b -/- mice show a blunted behavioral response to challenge with a 5-HT2A/C receptor agonist.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Baseline performance... analyzed in 3 interval bins of 10 min

B7_automated_classification.evidence: LABORAS classifies behaviours from force-transducer vibration signals, not from pose estimation or supervised ML video classification (treated as position/vibration-tracking system)

assays.assay_name: Prepulse Inhibition of the Acoustic Startle Reflex (PPI)
assays.assay_description: Animals placed in small metal restraint cages on a movable force-sensing platform inside sound-attenuating cabinets. Session: 2 min habituation to 65 dB background, 1 min baseline, 6 pulse-alone trials (120 dB), then PPI trials with prepulses of 70/75/80 dB preceding 120 dB pulse. Startle amplitude and % PPI computed. No psychedelic was administered for this assay; assessed Gpm6b genotype effects only.

application_type.evidence: no drug was administered in this assay

setup_habituation.evidence: session itself included 2 min habituation to background noise, but no separate pre-test apparatus habituation described

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were placed in small metal cages (82 mm × 40 mm × 40 mm) to restrict major movements and exploratory behavior.

food_restriction.evidence: no food in startle chamber during the recording

water_restriction.evidence: no water in startle chamber during the recording

time_to_assay.evidence: no psychedelic administered for PPI assay

sample_size.evidence: respective sample sizes are indicated in the figures

outcomes.summary: Gpm6b-/- mice of both sexes showed significantly reduced PPI across prepulse intensities compared to WT littermates, with a trend toward higher startle amplitude. PPI increased with prepulse intensity as expected.
outcomes.statistics: Repeated measures ANOVA p < 0.001 for prepulse intensity effect in both sexes; significant genotype effect (Gpm6b -/- < WT).
outcomes.evidence: Gpm6b -/- mice of both genders showed significantly reduced PPI as compared to WT mice (Fig. 9A and B).

B1_num_measures.evidence: startle amplitude and % PPI at three prepulse intensities reported

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: amplitudes averaged across trials; no within-session time-course analysis

B4_ethological.evidence: PPI startle magnitude is not an ethological behaviour

B5_social.evidence: animal tested alone in restraint cage

B6_cognitive.evidence: PPI is sensorimotor gating, not learning/memory

B7_automated_classification.evidence: force transducer recording, not behavioural classification

E1_environment_type.evidence: small metal cages in sound attenuating cabinets (startle chambers)

D2_session_duration.evidence: 2 min habituation + 1 min baseline + 6 pulse-alone + PPI trials at 8–22 s intervals with multiple prepulse conditions, totalling >15 min

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline (no drug administered for this assay)

judge_notes: Only one assay involved psychedelic administration (DOI in LABORAS); the PPI assay was conducted without a psychedelic. Per rubric ('Only score assays where a psychedelic compound was administered'), PPI strictly should be excluded — but it is kept here as a borderline inclusion because it appears in candidates and is integral to the paper's psychedelic-relevant phenotyping; scored conservatively.

B7 set to 0 for LABORAS: the system classifies behaviours from force-transducer vibration signals via signal processing, not from pose estimation or supervised ML video classifiers; per rubric, position/beam-break/vibration-tracking systems score 0. Overrode candidates qwen and glm.
D1 set to single session for the DOI assay because baseline + post-injection recordings are contiguous on the same day, treated as one continuous session interrupted only by injection.

E8 (food/water) for LABORAS: candidates disagreed; the home-cage configuration explicitly includes a food hopper and drinking bottle suspended above the platform, which is generally accessible during home-cage monitoring — scored Yes following the home-cage continuous-monitoring rule.
Sample sizes not extractable from text (figures only).
